title: Dataset structure and duplicate handling
caption: Original records, within-file exact deduplication and conservative cross-resolution record grouping. All original CSVs were preserved. Group counts are not verified specimen counts. One representative per group and resolution was used in the final protocol. Exact duplicate removal uses numeric equality, without rounding or a similarity threshold.
placement: Materials and methods 2.1, after the dataset description.

title: Preprocessed spectra on the common physical grid
caption: Per-polymer median spectra with 10th–90th percentile bands across the paired record representatives, shown for descriptive purposes only. Display summaries do not fit preprocessing or classifiers and use all analysis records. Spectral direction is conventional high-to-low wavenumber. Stored absorbance/transmittance semantics were not verified; the ordinate denotes the numeric preprocessed signal.

title: Frozen representation and 4+1+1 protocol
caption: Representation fitting and source-only validation precede class registration. Base reference groups are sampled from legal base-training groups, not from a mutually disjoint extra support split. Novel support/query pools and all evaluation queries remain group-disjoint from representation training/selection. The first novel class is HDPE, PP or PET for the three tasks; the second is LDPE, PS or PVC, respectively.

title: Conventional and class-statistical baselines
caption: Final-session 5/10-shot means for spectrum 1-NN/SVM, frozen PCA128 and EP-M1 with shrinkage. Error bars are descriptive SD across nine task–seed means, not standard errors or confidence intervals. The seeds/tasks share data; repeated episodes are not independent specimens. The ordinate starts at 55%. SVM is refitted on the permitted retained reference bank.

title: Representations under the fixed shrinkage head
caption: PCA64/PCA128, CE-M1-128 and EP-M1-128 with the same numerical shrinkage rule. Final-session primary 5/10-shot results; error bars are descriptive SD over nine dependent task–seed means. Axes start at 60%. Equal dimensions or a common numeric ridge do not equalise feature scales or relative regularisation.
placement: Results 4.2 / Table 3; PCA64 control also supports Results 4.6.

title: Episodic versus CE training at a fixed distance head
caption: Paired differences in final-session overall and combined novel-class accuracy. Each unit averages 200 paired repeats and the primary 5/10 shots. Points show the mean, error bars descriptive SD across nine dependent task–seed units. The training contrast also changes sampling roles and validation objectives; it is not an isolated pure-loss causal experiment.
placement: Results 4.2, after the negative finding about Euclidean novel recognition.

title: Distance-head ablation on the same frozen EP encoder
caption: Only the inference head changes: squared Euclidean, independent class full covariance with ridge .001, or class-specific shrinkage with tau5 and the fixed legal source prior. Overall accuracy and novel accuracy can move in opposite directions, notably in C/D. Error bars show descriptive task–seed SD.

title: Recognition versus novel support size
caption: All prespecified novel support sizes, 1/5/10/20, using nested support prefixes and the same query draws. Curves are means over task–seed units; their connecting lines aid reading and are not fitted performance models. No support size was selected after inspection.
placement: Results 4.3–4.4; use as supplementary if main text space is limited.

title: Base and novel recognition across incremental sessions
caption: EP-M1 with shrinkage, primary 5/10-shot averages. The dashed first-novel curve follows the same first introduced class from session1 to session2, even though its stored state is unchanged. The combined novel curve averages one class in session1 and two classes in session2. No novel accuracy is defined in session0. Curves describe decision competition rather than encoder-update forgetting.

title: Effect of target-resolution base references
caption: Paired source-bank to target-bank transitions C→E and D→F. Thin lines show nine task–seed pairs and bold lines their means. Representation parameters and the source covariance prior are fixed. Target-aligned banks require 80 labelled target base references, a different data-access condition from C/D.

title: HDPE / LDPE held out: cross-resolution confusion
caption: Fixed 10-shot final session, three-seed pooled confusion, shown without selecting a best seed. Rows are true classes and columns predictions; each row sums to 100%. C/D retain source base references. Compare EP full/shrinkage and the dimension-matched PCA128 shrinkage reference. Asterisks mark genuine held-out classes. All six settings including target-aligned E/F are provided in the complete confusion supplement.
placement: Results 4.3–4.4; one page may move to supplementary material.

title: Exact M1 encoder architecture
caption: The locked multiscale M1 definition in encoder_architecture_models.py. The three convolutional branches preserve physical position; ordered spectral-bin pooling precedes the 128-dimensional embedding. CE uses an additional temporary four-class head (516 parameters) only during initial supervised training.

title: Six settings and data-access conditions
caption: The representation and covariance prior are source-trained and frozen in every setting. E/F use additional labelled target-resolution base references; gains over C/D are not free or label-free adaptation. Training uses all legal source base-training groups, whereas classifier reference banks use 20 spectra per base class and K per novel class.
placement: Experimental design 3.1; visual companion to Table 1.

title: Role counts under the three held-out class tasks
caption: Counts shown for seed0; class-wise role counts are identical across seeds although group membership changes. Base reference spectra are selected from base_train, so they are not an additional mutually disjoint split. Novel support/query pools remain separate; only K support groups and 15 query groups per seen class enter a given episode. C4/C8 counterparts inherit the same group role.

title: Feature scale and effective regularisation
caption: Source base-training embeddings only. Mean feature norm, effective rank of the pooled residual covariance and numeric ridge divided by mean residual variance. The last panel uses a logarithmic ordinate. A fixed ridge value does not impose equal relative regularisation on CE/EP representations; effective rank alone does not establish better novel-class recognition.

title: Recorded representation and class-update costs
caption: Descriptive timings from the archived runs, not a controlled speed benchmark. Initial neural training includes validation/checkpoint work, whereas PCA time covers fitting only. Incremental head times exclude encoding/preprocessing: PCA registers only the arriving class; SVM refits the entire retained labelled bank. Different runs and operation scopes prohibit interpreting the ratios as intrinsic algorithmic speedups.

title: Database file schema and evaluation manifests
caption: The actual CSV layout includes a separate physical-wavenumber metadata row. Duplicate mapping relates original rows to retained records; paired group indices address the loaded deduplicated arrays. Split/episode manifests express legal roles and matched draws. A CSV row index must not be treated as a cross-resolution specimen identity.
placement: Data-availability and reproducibility appendix; companion to Fig01.
